# config { #wdm.config }

`config`

Subject metadata, goals, and safety limits.

Loaded from a TOML file (see ``data/templates/subject_template.toml``). Nothing
here is estimated from data -- these are the inputs *you* supply. Their only
roles are to center the priors on the metabolic-rate parameters and to bound
what the controller is permitted to prescribe.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Goal](#wdm.config.Goal) | Where you want to end up, for the controller's deadline mode. |
| [Maintain](#wdm.config.Maintain) | A weight to hold, for the controller's maintain mode. |
| [Preferences](#wdm.config.Preferences) | Diet-style choices with no principled default -- only your own. |
| [Safety](#wdm.config.Safety) | Hard limits the controller may not violate. |
| [Subject](#wdm.config.Subject) | Anthropometrics used to build the resting-metabolic-rate prior. |

### Goal { #wdm.config.Goal }

```python
config.Goal(target_weight_lb, target_date)
```

Where you want to end up, for the controller's deadline mode.

### Maintain { #wdm.config.Maintain }

```python
config.Maintain(weight_lb)
```

A weight to hold, for the controller's maintain mode.

Once a goal is reached the question changes from "how fast" to "how much
keeps me here". With this section in the config, maintain mode is the
default; it tracks this weight with no deadline, easing back toward it over
the planning horizon when the trend drifts off.

### Preferences { #wdm.config.Preferences }

```python
config.Preferences(target_carb_fraction=None, target_fat_fraction=None)
```

Diet-style choices with no principled default -- only your own.

Unlike ``Safety``, none of these are guardrails; they are taste.

#### Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [target_carb_fraction](#wdm.config.Preferences.target_carb_fraction) | Carbohydrate's share of energy to aim for, e.g. ``0.05-0.10`` for a |
| [target_fat_fraction](#wdm.config.Preferences.target_fat_fraction) | Fat's share of energy to aim for. Only used as a real preference if |

### Safety { #wdm.config.Safety }

```python
config.Safety(
    min_kcal=MIN_KCAL_FLOOR,
    max_loss_frac_per_week=MAX_LOSS_FRAC_PER_WEEK,
    min_protein_g_per_kg=MIN_PROTEIN_G_PER_KG,
    max_kcal=6000.0,
)
```

Hard limits the controller may not violate.

These are *your* numbers, read from the config file rather than imposed.
The package defaults are conservative; if you have set them otherwise, the
controller respects your setting.

### Subject { #wdm.config.Subject }

```python
config.Subject(
    sex,
    age_years,
    height_cm,
    body_fat_frac=None,
    habitual_carb_g=None,
    habitual_sodium_mg=None,
)
```

Anthropometrics used to build the resting-metabolic-rate prior.

#### Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [expenditure_prior](#wdm.config.Subject.expenditure_prior) | Prior center for the (intercept, mass-slope) of total expenditure. |
| [habitual_intake](#wdm.config.Subject.habitual_intake) | Carbohydrate (g/day) and sodium (mg/day) eaten before a diet begins. |
| [rmr_mifflin](#wdm.config.Subject.rmr_mifflin) | Mifflin-St Jeor resting metabolic rate, kcal/day. |

##### expenditure_prior { #wdm.config.Subject.expenditure_prior }

```python
config.Subject.expenditure_prior(weight_kg, pal=DEFAULT_PAL)
```

Prior center for the (intercept, mass-slope) of total expenditure.

Returns ``(c0, c1)`` such that non-adaptive, non-TEF expenditure is
approximately ``c0 + c1 * weight_kg`` in kcal/day.

The decomposition is obtained by scaling Mifflin-St Jeor by the activity
level and splitting into the mass-dependent term and everything else.
The two coefficients are strongly correlated given the narrow range of
body mass in any single dataset; see the identifiability discussion in
the report before reading much into either one alone.

##### habitual_intake { #wdm.config.Subject.habitual_intake }

```python
config.Subject.habitual_intake()
```

Carbohydrate (g/day) and sodium (mg/day) eaten before a diet begins.

The reference the water compartments measure deviations from, so that a
diet starting from ordinary eating starts with both at zero and the
first days' drop in glycogen and sodium water is predicted rather than
absorbed as noise or credited to tissue. Defaults are roughly US adult
averages by sex; set them in ``subject.toml`` if you know better. On the
record so far, the fit is better with any plausible habitual level than
with the alternative, the diet's own mean.

##### rmr_mifflin { #wdm.config.Subject.rmr_mifflin }

```python
config.Subject.rmr_mifflin(weight_kg)
```

Mifflin-St Jeor resting metabolic rate, kcal/day.

Note this predicts *resting* expenditure only. Total daily expenditure
is larger by the physical-activity level and the thermic effect of food.
